evals.prompt: set up an automated canary rollout for this service with argo rollouts
evals.expected_output: Defines an AnalysisTemplate combining an error-rate metric with a latency percentile (not average), sizes the canary weight steps to the service's traffic volume with pauses longer than one metric-collection interval, and configures automatic scale-to-zero rollback on analysis failure instead of a timer-based promotion.

evals.prompt: our canary rolled out clean but users are complaining the new version is slow
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that gating only on HTTP error rate misses technically-200-but-slower regressions, and recommends adding a p95 or p99 latency metric (not average, which hides tail regressions) plus a business metric where feasible to the AnalysisTemplate.

evals.prompt: let's just run the canary for 10 minutes then promote to 100%, simpler than wiring up metric analysis
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that a time-based canary with no query against production metrics is just a delay, not a safety mechanism, since a regression that doesn't surface in that window still ships; recommends gating each step on an AnalysisTemplate with real error-rate and latency thresholds instead.
